children: Commodity markets traded mixed on September 1, with oil prices rising as renewed US-Iran fighting heightened concerns over supply disruptions, while gold steadied after a two-day decline.
Oil prices gained on Tuesday as the resumption of fighting between the U.S. and Iran in the Middle East renewed fears of supply disruptions from the world's key crude-producing region.
Brent crude futures were up 56 cents, or 0.6%, to $91.05 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude was up 83 cents, or 1%, to $86.59.
In the previous session, Brent closed up 2.7%, at one point reaching its highest since August 25, and WTI settled up 2.8%, touching its highest since August 21.

Gold steadied after a two-day drop as the US and Iran exchanged strikes for the first time in a month, raising the odds of rising energy costs pushing up inflation and pressuring the Federal Reserve to lift interest rates.

Bullion was trading around $4,445 an ounce, after falling more than 3.5% over the previous two sessions. American forces hit an island in the Strait of Hormuz and the Islamic Republic responded by launching attacks on the United Arab Emirates and Jordan.
Among other precious metals, silver was stable at $66.56 an ounce. Platinum and palladium were little changed.

The U.S. dollar was subdued, backing away from Friday's gains as investors contended with rising odds of a hike from the Federal Reserve in September after last week's hawkish remarks from Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh.

title: Commodity Corner: Oil rises on US-Iran tensions; gold steadies after two-day decline
